findings.claim: Adding two real EDGAR filings (19.47 MB) to `evals/heldout/fixtures/` silently invalidates the of-record sweep projection and five other counts in two documents of record, and the diff neither corrects them nor logs them as debt.
findings.evidence: `docs/analysis-report.md:553` ("the five held-out filings in `evals/heldout/fixtures/`" - there are now seven), `:893` ("the five held-out filings ... include the second-largest filing in the repo (`spg-2019`, 9.36 MiB)" - spg-2019 is now third behind c-2025 at 15.40 MiB and jpm-2024 at 12.25 MiB), `:902` the row marked ← of record (`real_edgar_committed | 33 | 2.104 MiB | 153 s | 1,072 s ≈ 18 min`), `:922` ("the 28 real dev fixtures plus the 5 held-out filings"). Same numbers in `specs/decisions/ADR-021-benchmark-instrument.md:211` - "`real_edgar_committed` still 33 / 2.104 MiB - **no real filing joined the corpus**", which this diff falsifies - plus `:214` and `:752`. `evals/bench.py:232 heldout_sizes()` reads the directory by `stat`, so the next bench run recomputes the population: 35 filings, mean (33*2.104 + 3.167 + 15.403)/35 = 2.514 MiB, a +19.5% move in the projection of record (153 s → ~183 s, 1,072 s → ~1,281 s ≈ 21 min). No eval case could have gone red on this: `src/repo_hygiene/eval_adapter.py` pins ADR headers and report-citation resolution, not population counts.
findings.repro: python3 -c "print((33*2.104 + 3320720/1048576 + 16150764/1048576)/35)"  # 2.5143 vs the 2.104 MiB printed at docs/analysis-report.md:902 and ADR-021:211,752; ls evals/heldout/fixtures | wc -l  # 7, against "five held-out filings"
findings.acceptance: Either the six stale statements are corrected (n=35, recomputed mean and sweep, spg-2019 no longer called second-largest, ADR-021 §b amended to record that two real filings joined) with a fresh bench artifact cited, or a Debt row in `tasks/TODO.md` names each stale location by file:line so the staleness is enumerated rather than latent - and ADR-021:211's "no real filing joined the corpus" is retracted either way.

findings.claim: The H4 write-up - the permanent record of the run it is the whole deliverable of - misstates the c-2025 result: it reports 22 items `missing` and "the one deviation" from the frozen prediction, when the committed report shows 21 `missing` and TWO items at `omitted`/0.75, so a second deviation from the frozen prediction goes unrecorded.
findings.evidence: `evals/report/20260826-005839-fast.json`, `c-2025-heldout.items_summary`: Counter({('missing', 0.4): 21, ('omitted', 0.75): 2}) - item 9C and item 16 are both `omitted` at 0.75. The frozen prediction in `evals/heldout/c-2025-heldout.json` provenance says "all 23 era items reported `missing` with null offsets at BASE_MISSING 0.40", so item 16 deviates from it exactly as 9C does. Three places state it wrong: `evals/heldout/README.md` H4 entry, commit message 353e8f1, and the `tasks/TODO.md` D6 row. This is the same class the README's own authoring-discipline section counts six times - an asserted number the artifact does not support - in a file whose stated purpose is that predictions cannot be retrofitted.
findings.repro: python3 -c "import json,collections; r=json.load(open('evals/report/20260826-005839-fast.json')); print(collections.Counter((i['status'],i['confidence']) for c in r['results'] if c['id']=='c-2025-heldout' for i in c['items_summary']))"
findings.acceptance: `evals/heldout/README.md` H4 and the `tasks/TODO.md` D6 row read 21 `missing` at 0.40 and TWO `omitted` at 0.75 (9C and 16), and name item 16 as the second deviation from the frozen prediction, noting that the case's own declination (a) called `omitted` "the natural reading" for 16, which the run then produced. Since 353e8f1 is pushed, the correction rides the next consolidated commit with its own honest message per CLAUDE.md rule 7.

findings.claim: The diff makes an unedited row of the file it edits false: `spg-2019`'s inventory row still says "second-largest anywhere here", contradicting the new `c-2025` row in the same table.

The row added by this diff says c-2025 is "16.1 MB, the largest file in either set" (16,150,764), and `evals/fixtures/README.md` lists `jpm-2024` at 12,849,180. spg-2019 is now third.

findings.claim: The c-2025 provenance's "exactly four hits" enumeration for its case-insensitive item-plus-digit scan is not reproducible; the load-bearing claim behind it is verified and holds, but the enumeration is wrong in both directions.
findings.evidence: `evals/heldout/c-2025-heldout.json` provenance: "A case-insensitive raw regex for item-plus-digit returns exactly four hits in the whole file ... the cover's combined pointer at raw offset 1,828,047, two Regulation S-K citations ('Item 402(v)' at 1,859,455 and 'Item 408' at 15,875,549), and one 'Reconciling Items' phrase." On the committed bytes `(?i)items?\s*[0-9]` returns 3 hits at exactly those three offsets; the named fourth ("Reconciling Items") contains no digit and cannot match an item-plus-digit regex, and the loosest reading `(?i)item[^<]{0,4}[0-9]` returns 8 - the five extras are `Items)”` (the digits come from the entity). The claims that matter - `Item 1.` 0x, `ITEM ` 0x, `FORM 10-K CROSS-REFERENCE INDEX` 1x, anchor 1x, `DISCLOSURE CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES` 2x, `December 31, 2025` 159x / floating-comma 0x - all reproduce exactly, as do every intc-2025 raw-byte and scan offset re-derived independently (23 codes exactly once each, scan len 571,466, index at 567,879, Risk Factors 232,331→328,627).
findings.acceptance: The provenance states the exact regex used and a hit count that regex actually produces on the committed bytes (3 for `items?\s*\d`), and drops or re-describes the "Reconciling Items" entry.

findings.claim: Two byte-level/index details in the intc-2025 provenance are off - a raw offset by 8 bytes, and the Item 1 and Item 7 page maps omit ranges the index actually lists.
findings.evidence: `evals/heldout/intc-2025-heldout.json` provenance: "The cover reads 'For the fiscal year ended December 27, 2025.' at raw offset 330847" - the literal starts at 330839. Same paragraph: "1 Business pages 3-5/3-24/33/52/72-75" and "7 MD&A 18-36", where the committed index reads "General development of business Pages 3 - 5 , 18", "Available information Page 2" and, for Item 7, "Critical accounting estimates Pages 34 - 36 , 65 - 72". The omissions do not change any asserted label (both items are floored at a deliberately loose 2,000 precisely because the ranges are discontiguous), but a held-out provenance is the document of record for the frozen reading.
findings.repro: python3 -c "b=open('evals/heldout/fixtures/intc-2025/filing.htm','rb').read();print(b.find(b'For the fiscal year ended December 27, 2025.'))"  # 330839
findings.acceptance: Offset corrected to 330839 and the Item 1 / Item 7 page maps quoted in full (or explicitly marked as an abridged quotation).

findings.claim: Neither new case asserts `doc_status`, and neither case's enumerated declination list mentions the omission - an undeclared drop of the exact signal the postmortem says lied at the demo.
findings.evidence: `evals/heldout/intc-2025-heldout.json` and `evals/heldout/c-2025-heldout.json` `expect.checks` contain no `doc_status` check; three of the five incumbent held-out cases do (`cost-2022`, `csco-2016`, `pgr-2023`). Both cases carry an explicit "WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT ASSERT" list (a)-(e) and `doc_status` appears in neither list. The run then produced `success_with_warning` on intc-2025 (23 stub items, 1,727 chars total) and `ambiguous` on c-2025, which is the postmortem §2 banner-vs-panel complaint the exam is meant to hold D8/D9/D11 to. The cases still fail on their floors, so this is not a green-scoring hole - it is an undeclared declination in a set whose discipline is that every declination is named.
findings.repro: python3 -c "import glob;[print(p.split('/')[-1], 'doc_status' in open(p).read()) for p in sorted(glob.glob('evals/heldout/*.json'))]"
findings.acceptance: Either a `doc_status` check is added, or the declination list gains an item saying `doc_status` is deliberately not asserted and why - matching the discipline the other five declinations already follow.

findings.claim: `intc-2025` is satisfiable by repairing 4 of its 23 items: the other 19 may stay as 20-to-226-char index-row stubs at `extracted`/0.95 and every remaining check still passes; declination (c) states a reason for excluding item 9A that the committed index contradicts.
findings.evidence: `evals/heldout/intc-2025-heldout.json` puts floors/anchors only on items 1, 1A, 7, 8; `expected_set_complete`, `only_items`, `known_items_only`, `verbatim`, `no_overlap_ordered`, `no_empty_success` and `deterministic` all passed on the fully-collapsed baseline (`evals/report/20260826-005839-fast.json`, only 5 red checks). Declination (c) justifies dropping boundaries for "items 2, 3, 5, 7A, 9A, 9B, 15, whose content the index scatters across single pages inside other sections" - which the committed index bears out for 3 (Pages 102-105, nested in item 8's 56-108) and 15 (56-108, 110-115), but NOT for 9A, whose index row is a lone contiguous "Page 109" outside every other item's range and therefore as floorable as 1A's 37-51. A D11 slow path that repairs exactly items 1/1A/7/8 and leaves 9A on its 43-char stub scores this exam green.
findings.acceptance: Prose half (repair, self-contradiction test): declination (c) must not state a reason the committed index contradicts. Floor half (a CHOICE, argue it either way in writing): add a 9A floor derived from the index alone, or state why not - and address explicitly whether adding an assertion after the baseline run contaminates the case under the burn rule.
